pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds a NOT NULL column with default 'normal' and a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the 3 seeded rows are normal and that setting 'urgent' throws.
The `item` function in src/index.js appends ' — priority' unless the priority is normal. Test 'AC-2' asserts the exact <li> text for high, normal and low items.
src/index.js filters with a bound `WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id`. Test 'AC-3' covers high, low and normal, including id order (rows 3 and 1 set to high, listed as 1 then 3).
The unfiltered query is `ORDER BY id`. Test 'AC-4' asserts the full ordered list.
The `nav` function renders the current filter as <strong> and the others as links. Test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav markup for all four views.

src/index.js returns 400 for a present but unlisted value, before any query, using a Set (so __proto__ is safe). Test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, checks the status, and checks there is no <li>.

src/index.js uses `No ${priority}-priority items.` when the table is non-empty and the filter matches nothing, and 'No items yet.' otherwise. Test 'AC-7' covers the high, low and normal messages and the empty table in all four views.

traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The test checks the file contents. The traffic Worker passes the path including the query to the app, and the check script and fake app were adjusted to accept a query.

findings.what: The README describes the ?priority= filter but not the new 400 response for any other value. It also doesn't mention that the page shows All/High/Normal/Low navigation.
findings.fix: Add a short clause saying other priority values answer 400.

findings.what: The AC-8 test only checks the contents of routes.json. It doesn't run the traffic Worker against the real app, so it doesn't prove the route returns 200.
findings.fix: Optional: also fetch each ROUTES entry through the app in a test and assert it returns 200.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing was added beyond the ask. The traffic-config-check relaxation to allow query strings is needed by AC-8 and the PR discloses it.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented, and each has a test that would fail if it were broken.

Tests assert rendered output and status codes. No tests were deleted. The traffic fake app and the config-check test were extended, not loosened, and the fragment and space rejections are still tested.
The README mentions the filter. The only gap is the 400 response, which is low severity.
The 400 check runs before the query, and the priority value is bound as a parameter. I found no defects. I could not run the tests because Bash was denied, so this is from reading only.

The query parameter is validated against an allowlist and bound in SQL. The title is HTML-escaped, and the priority value is only output after the allowlist check. I found no planted instructions in the repo content.
The diff changes a server-rendered HTML page, but I found no UI framework or design files. I'm treating it as having no designed UI, which is a judgement.
There is no browser flow or UI under test in this change, and the PR says no screenshots.

The title is under 72 characters, and the claims I could check match the diff: the behaviour, the migration, the routes and the config-check change. I did not check the 'tests deleted: none' claim against git history, because Bash was denied. The test files I read show no deletions.
